uncited: 2DGS modifies the primitive representation and projection pipeline of 3D Gaussian Splatting to enforce a zero-thickness, surface-aligned geometry.
*   **Outputs:** A set of $N$ 2D Gaussian primitives, each defined by position, orientation, scale, opacity, and color coefficients.
**Mean Position** ($\boldsymbol{\mu}_i$): A 3D vector $(x, y, z)$ in world space.
**Orientation** ($\mathbf{q}_i$): A quaternion representing the normal direction of the disk.
This replaces the full 3D rotation matrix $\mathbf{R}_i$ used in 3DGS, as the disk has rotational symmetry around its normal.
**Scale** ($\mathbf{s}_i$): A 2D vector $(s_{i,x}, s_{i,y})$ defining the extent of the disk in its local tangent plane.
The third dimension (thickness) is effectively zero.
**Appearance**: Spherical Harmonics (SH) coefficients for view-dependent color.
The 3D covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i$ is replaced by a 2D covariance structure.
The 2D Gaussian is defined in its local coordinate system where the $z$-axis aligns with the surface normal.
The 2D covariance matrix $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}'_i$ in screen space is computed by projecting the local 2D disk.
Let $\mathbf{W}$ be the view rotation matrix and $\mathbf{J}$ be the Jacobian of the projective transformation.
